card.description: A fixed CSS block built by evaluating the four binary coordinate functions on every nonzero point of F_2^4. Those evaluation rows are the X checks; their orthogonal complement after adjoining the all-one logical row supplies the Z checks. The resulting protected qubit corrects one arbitrary single-qubit error and admits a transversal non-Clifford phase, making this block both the switching partner of the Steane code and the algebraic core of 15-to-1 magic-state distillation.

views.description: Label the qubits by the fifteen nonzero four-bit strings. Evaluating each coordinate bit across those labels gives four independent weight-eight X checks. Appending the all-one evaluation selects the logical coset; the binary orthogonal complement then gives the ten Z checks.

The four X rows and ten Z rows form fourteen independent commuting symplectic generators. Their centralizer modulo their span leaves the all-one X representative paired with a weight-three Z representative; exact CSS enumeration finds no lighter nontrivial logical operator.

Put the odd all-one logical row above the four even X-check rows. Every pair and every triple has even overlap. The check-row coset has weight zero modulo eight, while its all-one complement has weight seven modulo eight; this fixes both transversality and the logical T-versus-T-dagger convention.

The same incidence data can be drawn as a tetrahedral three-dimensional color-code patch. Cells and faces make the check supports geometric; this is a dictionary for the Reed–Muller evaluation table, not a second stabilizer code with merely coincident parameters.

A common doubled-color-code subsystem exposes the Steane and fifteen-qubit blocks as different gauge choices. Measuring the checks that distinguish those choices turns code switching into a syndrome-conditioned operation rather than an unexplained change of stabilizer tables.

Regard the one-to-fifteen encoding isometry as a tensor with one logical leg and fifteen physical legs. Operator pushing recovers the same stabilizer and logical cosets, while contracting multiple copies creates a new code whose global parameters must be recomputed rather than inherited from this block.

The binary symplectic table records Pauli supports but discards the eighth-root phases accumulated by a transversal T-type layer. XP stabilizer notation retains those phases, making it a complementary language for diagonal logical action rather than a different origin for the code.

# Fifteen-qubit quantum Reed–Muller code

## Essence

**The object.** Label fifteen physical qubits by the nonzero vectors

`V* = F_2^4 \ {0000}`.

For each of the four coordinate bits, evaluate that bit on every label. The
four resulting length-fifteen rows form the X-check matrix `H_X`. Let `1`
denote the all-one row and define the Z-check space by

`row(H_Z) = span(H_X, 1)^perp`.

This prescription is the whole executable code. The X and Z ranks are four
and ten, so fourteen stabilizer constraints leave one logical qubit. A
three-point line `{a,b,a+b}` supports a logical Z; no Pauli of weight one or
two is logical. The shipped instance therefore recomputes `[[15,1,3]]`
exactly. The complete rank, quotient, and distance argument is on the
[punctured-evaluation](pedagogy/punctured-evaluation-css.md) and
[logical-distance](pedagogy/logical-quotient-and-distance.md) pages.

**The distinctive feature.** Put the odd all-one logical-X row above the four
even X checks. Every pair and every triple of these five rows has even
overlap. That stronger condition—triorthogonality—makes a bitwise T-type
phase preserve the code. In the logical convention fixed by the constructor,
physical `T` on all fifteen qubits implements logical `T^dagger`; physical
`T^dagger` implements logical `T`. The dagger is derived from codeword weights,
not chosen by naming convention; see the
[transversal-phase derivation](pedagogy/transversal-phase.md).

**One sentence.** The code is the punctured four-bit Boolean evaluation table
with one odd row reserved for the logical qubit: ordinary orthogonality makes
it a CSS code, and triple-overlap parity upgrades one diagonal physical layer
to a logical non-Clifford phase.

## Design problem

A CSS matrix only asks every X-check support to overlap every Z-check support
evenly. That guarantees commutation, but it says almost nothing about a
non-Clifford diagonal gate: applying `T` to a superposition gives each basis
word a phase determined by its weight modulo eight. If different words in the
same logical basis state acquire different phases, the state leaves the code
space even though every Pauli check still commutes.

The fifteen-qubit construction solves both constraints with one Boolean
table. A nonzero linear function on `F_2^4` is balanced: among the sixteen
points it is one on eight, and puncturing `0000` does not change that support.
Thus every nonzero X-stabilizer word has weight eight. Distinct coordinate
functions overlap on four points; three distinct coordinate functions overlap
on two. Those powers of two are exactly the divisibility data needed by a
T-type phase.

The price is visible in the same table:

- the block is fixed at fifteen physical qubits and distance three, so it is
  not by itself a scaling memory family;
- the protected directions are asymmetric: the minimum X-logical weight is
  seven while the minimum Z-logical weight is three;
- bitwise H exchanges four X constraints with ten Z constraints, so H does
  not preserve this unchanged stabilizer presentation;
- a transversal non-Clifford layer is only a block operation. State
  preparation, syndrome extraction, switching, decoding, acceptance, and
  routing remain protocol costs.

This is why the block appears in two complementary workflows. A distillation
factory uses its parity checks to reject likely input magic-state faults. A
code-switching protocol moves a logical state between this block, where the
T-type phase is transversal, and Steane, where the Clifford symmetry is
better. The [protocol and evidence ledger](pedagogy/distillation-switching-realizations.md)
keeps those workflows separate.

## Derivation chain

**1. Puncture the zero coordinate.** Start from all sixteen vectors of
`F_2^4`, then remove `0000`. The remaining labels, in binary integer order
`0001, 0010, ..., 1111`, are the physical qubits. Each coordinate function
vanishes at `0000`, so its weight remains eight after puncturing.

**2. Reserve the odd row.** The four coordinate rows span a dimension-four
space `L`. The all-one row is not in `L`: every nonzero word in `L` has weight
eight, whereas `1` has weight fifteen. Use `L` for X stabilizers and reserve
`1+L` as the logical-X coset.

**3. Define Z checks by the exact orthogonal complement.** Take

`row(H_Z) = (L + span{1})^perp`.

Every Z row is orthogonal to every X row, so the CSS checks commute. The space
inside the perpendicular has dimension `15-5=10`; with `rank(H_X)=4`, the
encoded dimension is `15-4-10=1`. The basis printed by `constructor.py` is a
deterministic nullspace basis, but the code depends on its row space rather
than on those ten particular generators.

**4. Read the two logical sectors.** An X operator commuting with all Z checks
has support in `L + span{1}`. Modulo X stabilizers, the only nontrivial coset
is `1+L`; its words have weight fifteen or seven. A Z operator commuting with
all X checks has a support whose labels XOR to zero. The additional all-one
orthogonality defining Z stabilizers selects the even-weight part, so the odd
part is the logical-Z coset. Three distinct labels `a`, `b`, and `a+b` XOR to
zero and give a weight-three logical Z. The
[sector-distance proof](pedagogy/logical-quotient-and-distance.md) also rules
out weights one and two.

**5. Strengthen pairwise orthogonality to triple orthogonality.** In the
five-row matrix `G=[1; H_X]`, an all-one/coordinate pair overlaps on eight
qubits, two coordinate rows overlap on four, an all-one/two-coordinate triple
overlaps on four, and three coordinate rows overlap on two. Every count is
even, so `G` is triorthogonal.

**6. Fix the logical phase.** The X-stabilizer superposition for `|0_L>`
contains one word of weight zero and fifteen of weight eight. Its all-one
complement, representing `|1_L>`, contains one word of weight fifteen and
fifteen of weight seven. Bitwise physical `T` therefore gives every
`|0_L>` component phase `1` and every `|1_L>` component phase
`exp(-i pi/4)`. That is logical `T^dagger` up to a common phase.

**7. Separate algebra from protocol.** The same X-check equations can be used
as an accept/reject test for phase faults in an idealized 15-to-1 block. They
do not specify a factory circuit. Likewise, a relation between Steane and
Reed–Muller stabilizer groups does not specify a fault-tolerant switching
schedule. The [decoder/circuit page](pedagogy/decoding-and-circuits.md) and
[protocol ledger](pedagogy/distillation-switching-realizations.md) name the
missing layers explicitly.

## Multiple pictures

- **Boolean evaluation.** A qubit is a nonzero four-bit input, an X check is a
  coordinate function, and a Z support is a set of inputs whose vector sum is
  zero. This is the shortest route from labels to executable matrices.

- **CSS quotient.** Write `L=row(H_X)`. Then X normalizers are
  `L + span{1}`, while Z normalizers are `L^perp`. Stabilizers quotient out
  `L` in the X sector and the even-weight subspace of `L^perp` in the Z
  sector. This picture makes one encoded qubit and the `d_X=7`, `d_Z=3`
  asymmetry explicit. The shared
  [CSS chain-complex dictionary](../../foundations/css-chain-complexes/intuition.md)
  explains how such row-space quotients fit the Atlas convention.

- **Triorthogonal matrix.** The five rows `[1; H_X]` remember more than CSS
  commutation: pair and triple intersections are even. This is the useful
  picture for diagonal gates and magic-state distillation. A sign-free
  symplectic tableau alone cannot determine the accumulated eighth-root
  phases.

- **Tetrahedral 3D color code.** The same block admits a tetrahedral
  three-dimensional color-code realization in which cells, faces, and
  boundaries organize the supports. The landing visual is deliberately only
  a stabilizer-incidence scene; its circular layout is not a tetrahedron and
  does not claim spatial locality. The geometric equivalence is a curated
  literature dictionary, while the displayed incidence is constructor data.

- **Gauge-fixed double.** A larger subsystem description contains the Steane
  and fifteen-qubit blocks as different gauge choices. Measuring one set of
  checks or the other explains code switching as a syndrome-conditioned gauge
  decision rather than a magical replacement of matrices.

- **Tensor and XP views.** The encoding isometry can be used as a tensor whose
  operator-pushing rules recover stabilizers and logicals; contracting copies
  produces new global codes that need new parameter checks. XP notation keeps
  phase information beyond Pauli supports and is therefore useful for the
  diagonal action. Neither view changes the historical Reed–Muller origin.

The guided [incidence tour](../../tours/quantum_reed_muller_15.html) lets the
reader move from four-bit labels to X checks, the orthogonal Z space, the
logical quotient, and triorthogonality without confusing graph layout with
physical geometry.

## Why these parameters

**Why fifteen physical qubits.** There are sixteen inputs to a four-variable
Boolean function. Removing the zero input leaves `2^4-1=15` nonzero labels.
This puncture turns the all-one row into an odd-weight logical candidate while
leaving coordinate-function supports at weight eight.

**Why one logical qubit.** The four coordinate rows are independent. Adding
the independent all-one row gives a dimension-five space, whose orthogonal
complement has dimension ten. The CSS stabilizer rank is therefore
`4+10=14`, so `k=15-14=1`.

**Why total distance three.** A single label cannot sum to zero because zero
was punctured. Two distinct labels cannot sum to zero over `F_2`; equality
would be required. Thus there is no weight-one or weight-two Z normalizer.
For any distinct nonzero `a` and `b`, the three labels `a`, `b`, and `a+b`
are nonzero and distinct, and their sum is zero. Their odd cardinality keeps
the support outside the Z-stabilizer space, producing a logical Z of weight
three. Exact CSS enumeration independently returns three.

**Why the X distance is seven.** Every nonzero linear function is one on
eight of the fifteen labels. Complementing it by the all-one logical row gives
weight seven; complementing the zero function gives weight fifteen. Hence the
nontrivial X coset has minimum weight seven. The scalar distance records the
smaller sector, `min(7,3)=3`, so a bare `[[15,1,3]]` label hides useful bias
information.

**Why a T-type phase works.** The X-stabilizer words have weight zero modulo
eight, whereas every logical-one word has weight seven modulo eight. A
bitwise eighth-root phase is therefore constant within each logical basis
state but different between them. Pair and triple overlap parity is the local
row test for that global weight-divisibility statement.

All structured `n`, `k`, `d`, and CSS claims in `instances.yaml` are marked
`verified`; this entry uses no bounded distance and no claimed numeric code
parameter.

## Failure modes

- **Reading total distance as symmetric protection.** Distance three means the
  lightest nontrivial Pauli is weight three. It does not say both pure sectors
  have weight-three logicals. Here `d_Z=3` and `d_X=7` in the declared CSS
  convention. A decoder or biased-noise claim that ignores the sector is
  underspecified.

- **Treating a fixed block as a threshold family.** `constructor.py` has no
  size parameter. As of the 2026-08-02 decoder sweep, no source supports an
  intrinsic asymptotic threshold for this single block. Threshold language
  requires a growing Reed–Muller family, concatenation level, or full factory
  family together with its circuit, decoder, observable, and noise
  normalization.

- **Equating perfect-syndrome lookup with fault-tolerant recovery.** The four
  X-check outcomes directly address a single Z error by its four-bit qubit
  label. A circuit fault can instead create a correlated data error and alter
  a flag, preparation check, or conversion syndrome. The decision rule must
  consume the history produced by that circuit; see
  [decoding and circuits](pedagogy/decoding-and-circuits.md).

- **Dropping the dagger.** With the entry's `|0_L>,|1_L>` basis, physical
  `T^otimes 15` is logical `T^dagger`, not logical `T`. Reversing the physical
  layer reverses the logical gate. A source using the conjugate magic-state
  convention may name the layer oppositely, so the codeword phase is the
  invariant statement.

- **Calling the incidence circle a 3D lattice.** The generic widget shows
  exact qubit/check incidence and exact labels. It does not encode tetrahedral
  cells, boundaries, metric distance, or a hardware embedding. The 3D picture
  is literature-backed and awaits a general higher-dimensional cell-complex
  representation rather than a code-specific drawing disguised as formal
  data.

- **Calling transversal equal to universal or free.** The unchanged block has
  a transversal T-type phase and inter-block CNOT, but not a universal
  transversal set. Switching imports another code; distillation imports noisy
  resource states and postselection; both require extraction, decoding, and
  routing. The operation name must not erase those costs.

## Operations story

**Diagonal phase.** For a computational-basis word `x`, bitwise physical `T`
contributes `exp(i pi |x|/4)`. The two logical cosets have weights `0 mod 8`
and `7 mod 8`, respectively, so the induced diagonal is
`diag(1, exp(-i pi/4))`: logical `T^dagger`. The inverse physical layer gives
logical `T`. The [phase page](pedagogy/transversal-phase.md) checks this both
by overlap parities and by complete coset enumeration.

**Inter-block CNOT.** Pair corresponding qubits in two identically ordered
blocks. The usual CSS conjugation maps control X checks forward and target Z
checks backward while preserving both stabilizer groups, and it induces
logical CNOT on the paired quotients. This is one abstract entangling layer;
hardware routing and subsequent error correction are additional.

**Hadamard through switching.** Bitwise H would exchange a rank-four X space
with a rank-ten Z space, so it does not preserve this presentation. A
fault-tolerant route converts the state to Steane, uses Steane's transversal
H, and converts back. The conversion checks, repeated extraction,
syndrome-conditioned Pauli frame, and rejected runs belong to the H cost.

**15-to-1 distillation.** Under the ideal-Clifford, independent input
phase-error model, accept exactly the error supports in `ker(H_X)`. Accepted
supports of odd weight are logical failures. Their exact enumerator begins
with thirty-five weight-three supports, so the conditional output error begins
at third order; this is a recomputed block model, not a circuit-level factory
threshold. The full enumerator and acceptance denominator are on the
[protocol ledger](pedagogy/distillation-switching-realizations.md).

**What hardware has established.** A trapped-ion experiment prepared a
fifteen-qubit resource, switched it to Steane, and certified the accepted
logical magic state. A neutral-atom architecture used 3D fifteen-qubit blocks
as teleportation and angle-synthesis resources among other codes and qubit
reuse. These are operation-level demonstrations, not increasing-distance
Reed–Muller memory scaling; the exact claim boundaries and dates are retained
on the [evidence ledger](pedagogy/distillation-switching-realizations.md).

## Litmus questions

**Q1:** Why are the X checks weight eight after the zero point is removed?
**A:** Every nonzero linear function on all sixteen four-bit inputs is balanced
with eight ones, and every coordinate function evaluates to zero at `0000`.
Puncturing that point removes a zero, so the weight stays eight.

**Q2:** Why does `rank(H_Z)=10` rather than eleven? **A:** Z checks are
orthogonal to the four X rows and also to the independent all-one logical-X
row. Those five independent constraints on fifteen bits leave a
ten-dimensional orthogonal complement.

**Q3:** Give a logical Z without consulting the printed nullspace basis.
**A:** Choose two distinct nonzero labels `a` and `b`; support Z on
`{a,b,a+b}`. The three labels XOR to zero, so the operator commutes with every
coordinate X check. Its support has odd size, so it is not orthogonal to the
all-one row and therefore is not a Z stabilizer.

**Q4:** If the code distance is three, why is the minimum logical X weight
seven? **A:** The scalar distance is the minimum across Pauli sectors. The
logical-X coset is `1+L`, whose words have weights seven or fifteen, while the
logical-Z coset contains the three-point lines. Thus `d=min(d_X,d_Z)=3` with
`d_X=7` and `d_Z=3`.

**Q5:** Does physical T on every qubit implement logical T? **A:** Not in this
entry's basis. Logical-zero components have weight `0 mod 8`, while
logical-one components have weight `7 mod 8`; physical T therefore produces
logical `T^dagger`. Physical `T^dagger` produces logical T.

**Q6:** What extra evidence is needed before the incidence tour becomes a
fault-tolerant factory claim? **A:** At minimum: a preparation and extraction
circuit, fault locations and noise normalization, the syndrome/flag history
given to a decoder, acceptance and correction rules, and the logical failure
observable. The tour verifies stabilizer incidence and phase algebra only.

  phase information beyond Pauli supports and is therefore useful for the
  diagonal action. Neither view changes the historical Reed–Muller origin.

The guided [incidence tour](../../tours/quantum_reed_muller_15.html) lets the
reader move from four-bit labels to X checks, the orthogonal Z space, the
logical quotient, and triorthogonality without confusing graph layout with
physical geometry.

## Why these parameters

**Why fifteen physical qubits.** There are sixteen inputs to a four-variable
Boolean function. Removing the zero input leaves `2^4-1=15` nonzero labels.
This puncture turns the all-one row into an odd-weight logical candidate while
leaving coordinate-function supports at weight eight.

**Why one logical qubit.** The four coordinate rows are independent. Adding
the independent all-one row gives a dimension-five space, whose orthogonal
complement has dimension ten. The CSS stabilizer rank is therefore
`4+10=14`, so `k=15-14=1`.

**Why total distance three.** A single label cannot sum to zero because zero
was punctured. Two distinct labels cannot sum to zero over `F_2`; equality
would be required. Thus there is no weight-one or weight-two Z normalizer.
For any distinct nonzero `a` and `b`, the three labels `a`, `b`, and `a+b`
are nonzero and distinct, and their sum is zero. Their odd cardinality keeps
the support outside the Z-stabilizer space, producing a logical Z of weight
three. Exact CSS enumeration independently returns three.

**Why the X distance is seven.** Every nonzero linear function is one on
eight of the fifteen labels. Complementing it by the all-one logical row gives
weight seven; complementing the zero function gives weight fifteen. Hence the
nontrivial X coset has minimum weight seven. The scalar distance records the
smaller sector, `min(7,3)=3`, so a bare `[[15,1,3]]` label hides useful bias
information.

**Why a T-type phase works.** The X-stabilizer words have weight zero modulo
eight, whereas every logical-one word has weight seven modulo eight. A
bitwise eighth-root phase is therefore constant within each logical basis
state but different between them. Pair and triple overlap parity is the local
row test for that global weight-divisibility statement.

All structured `n`, `k`, `d`, and CSS claims in `instances.yaml` are marked
`verified`; this entry uses no bounded distance and no claimed numeric code
parameter.

## Failure modes

- **Reading total distance as symmetric protection.** Distance three means the
  lightest nontrivial Pauli is weight three. It does not say both pure sectors
  have weight-three logicals. Here `d_Z=3` and `d_X=7` in the declared CSS
  convention. A decoder or biased-noise claim that ignores the sector is
  underspecified.

- **Treating a fixed block as a threshold family.** `constructor.py` has no
  size parameter. As of the 2026-08-02 decoder sweep, no source supports an
  intrinsic asymptotic threshold for this single block. Threshold language
  requires a growing Reed–Muller family, concatenation level, or full factory
  family together with its circuit, decoder, observable, and noise
  normalization.

- **Equating perfect-syndrome lookup with fault-tolerant recovery.** The four
  X-check outcomes directly address a single Z error by its four-bit qubit
  label. A circuit fault can instead create a correlated data error and alter
  a flag, preparation check, or conversion syndrome. The decision rule must
  consume the history produced by that circuit; see
  [decoding and circuits](pedagogy/decoding-and-circuits.md).

- **Dropping the dagger.** With the entry's `|0_L>,|1_L>` basis, physical
  `T^otimes 15` is logical `T^dagger`, not logical `T`. Reversing the physical
  layer reverses the logical gate. A source using the conjugate magic-state
  convention may name the layer oppositely, so the codeword phase is the
  invariant statement.

- **Calling the incidence circle a 3D lattice.** The generic widget shows
  exact qubit/check incidence and exact labels. It does not encode tetrahedral
  cells, boundaries, metric distance, or a hardware embedding. The 3D picture
  is literature-backed and awaits a general higher-dimensional cell-complex
  representation rather than a code-specific drawing disguised as formal
  data.

- **Calling transversal equal to universal or free.** The unchanged block has
  a transversal T-type phase and inter-block CNOT, but not a universal
  transversal set. Switching imports another code; distillation imports noisy
  resource states and postselection; both require extraction, decoding, and
  routing. The operation name must not erase those costs.

## Operations story

**Diagonal phase.** For a computational-basis word `x`, bitwise physical `T`
contributes `exp(i pi |x|/4)`. The two logical cosets have weights `0 mod 8`
and `7 mod 8`, respectively, so the induced diagonal is
`diag(1, exp(-i pi/4))`: logical `T^dagger`. The inverse physical layer gives
logical `T`. The [phase page](pedagogy/transversal-phase.md) checks this both
by overlap parities and by complete coset enumeration.

**Inter-block CNOT.** Pair corresponding qubits in two identically ordered
blocks. The usual CSS conjugation maps control X checks forward and target Z
checks backward while preserving both stabilizer groups, and it induces
logical CNOT on the paired quotients. This is one abstract entangling layer;
hardware routing and subsequent error correction are additional.

**Hadamard through switching.** Bitwise H would exchange a rank-four X space
with a rank-ten Z space, so it does not preserve this presentation. A
fault-tolerant route converts the state to Steane, uses Steane's transversal
H, and converts back. The conversion checks, repeated extraction,
syndrome-conditioned Pauli frame, and rejected runs belong to the H cost.

**15-to-1 distillation.** Under the ideal-Clifford, independent input
phase-error model, accept exactly the error supports in `ker(H_X)`. Accepted
supports of odd weight are logical failures. Their exact enumerator begins
with thirty-five weight-three supports, so the conditional output error begins
at third order; this is a recomputed block model, not a circuit-level factory
threshold. The full enumerator and acceptance denominator are on the
[protocol ledger](pedagogy/distillation-switching-realizations.md).

**What hardware has established.** A trapped-ion experiment prepared a
fifteen-qubit resource, switched it to Steane, and certified the accepted
logical magic state. A neutral-atom architecture used 3D fifteen-qubit blocks
as teleportation and angle-synthesis resources among other codes and qubit
reuse. These are operation-level demonstrations, not increasing-distance
Reed–Muller memory scaling; the exact claim boundaries and dates are retained
on the [evidence ledger](pedagogy/distillation-switching-realizations.md).

## Litmus questions

**Q1:** Why are the X checks weight eight after the zero point is removed?
**A:** Every nonzero linear function on all sixteen four-bit inputs is balanced
with eight ones, and every coordinate function evaluates to zero at `0000`.
Puncturing that point removes a zero, so the weight stays eight.

**Q2:** Why does `rank(H_Z)=10` rather than eleven? **A:** Z checks are
orthogonal to the four X rows and also to the independent all-one logical-X
row. Those five independent constraints on fifteen bits leave a
ten-dimensional orthogonal complement.

**Q3:** Give a logical Z without consulting the printed nullspace basis.
**A:** Choose two distinct nonzero labels `a` and `b`; support Z on
`{a,b,a+b}`. The three labels XOR to zero, so the operator commutes with every
coordinate X check. Its support has odd size, so it is not orthogonal to the
all-one row and therefore is not a Z stabilizer.

**Q4:** If the code distance is three, why is the minimum logical X weight
seven? **A:** The scalar distance is the minimum across Pauli sectors. The
logical-X coset is `1+L`, whose words have weights seven or fifteen, while the
logical-Z coset contains the three-point lines. Thus `d=min(d_X,d_Z)=3` with
`d_X=7` and `d_Z=3`.

**Q5:** Does physical T on every qubit implement logical T? **A:** Not in this
entry's basis. Logical-zero components have weight `0 mod 8`, while
logical-one components have weight `7 mod 8`; physical T therefore produces
logical `T^dagger`. Physical `T^dagger` produces logical T.

**Q6:** What extra evidence is needed before the incidence tour becomes a
fault-tolerant factory claim? **A:** At minimum: a preparation and extraction
circuit, fault locations and noise normalization, the syndrome/flag history
given to a decoder, acceptance and correction rules, and the logical failure
observable. The tour verifies stabilizer incidence and phase algebra only.

documents.title: Perfect syndromes versus circuit decoding
documents.markdown:
# Perfect syndromes versus circuit decoding

> **Question.** If the block has only fifteen qubits and distance three, why
> are lookup decoding, flagged preparation, code switching, and AutDEC four
> different decoder claims?

A decoder consumes a specified classical record produced by a specified
noise and measurement process. Changing that record changes the inference
problem even when the final data block has the same stabilizer matrix.

## 1. The direct four-bit address for Z errors

For a Z error on the qubit labeled `v`, the X-check syndrome is

`H_X e_v^T = v`.

Because the qubit set contains every nonzero four-bit vector exactly once,
the fifteen possible one-qubit Z errors give all fifteen nonzero four-bit
syndromes. The syndrome is literally the binary qubit label. This is the
clean Hamming-style address table inherited from the evaluation matrix.

A zero syndrome after perfect measurement means either no Z component or a
higher-weight support in the X-check kernel; it does not prove the data is
error-free.

## 2. The ten-bit table for X errors

An X error is detected by the ten chosen Z generators. Its syndrome is the
corresponding column of `H_Z`. The nullspace algorithm fixes this ten-bit
basis deterministically, but those ten bits do not carry an invariant
four-bit geometric name: row-recombining the Z generators changes the
syndrome coordinates without changing the code.

For the shipped basis, all fifteen columns are nonzero and distinct. A zero
column would be an undetected weight-one X operator; equal columns would make
their weight-two difference undetected. Either outcome would contradict the
exact pure-X distance seven. A finite table can therefore locate every
one-qubit X error. A Y error activates both tables at the same physical
location.

This perfect-syndrome lookup corrects every arbitrary one-qubit Pauli error.
It makes no promise for an untrusted extraction circuit or multiple data
faults.

## 3. Why the circuit record is larger than a syndrome

Measuring a high-weight stabilizer couples ancillas to several data qubits.
An ancilla fault of the propagating Pauli type can spread through later gates
and create a correlated data error. A final block syndrome alone may not say
where in the circuit that fault occurred.

Different protocols preserve different side information:

- a **flagged preparation** supplies flag outcomes and preparation-check
  results in addition to the final syndrome;
- a **Steane/Reed–Muller conversion** supplies the sequence of measured gauge
  or conversion checks and may repeat them before choosing a Pauli frame;
- a **postselected distillation block** supplies an accept/reject syndrome and
  conditions whether any output exists;
- a **repeated memory** supplies a time history whose detector events depend
  on the extraction schedule.

The card keeps these regimes in separate decoder rows. Chamberland and Cross
analyze flag-assisted logical-state preparation
([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.00566)); Anderson, Duclos-Cianci, and
Poulin give an explicit switching decoder
([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.2734)); and Butt et al. retain
device-motivated preparation, verification, and postselection choices in
their switching comparison
([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.17686)).

## 4. AutDEC and BP-OSD live at another comparison level

Automorphism ensemble decoding runs a base belief-propagation decoder on
symmetry-permuted versions of a quantum-code problem and selects among the
candidate outputs. Koutsioumpas et al. compare this with BP-OSD on quantum
Reed–Muller blocks under code-capacity noise and perfect syndrome
([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.01738)).

That result does not automatically decode a flagged preparation or switching
circuit. A circuit-level adapter would need to define ancilla faults,
measurement faults, correlations, detector construction, the supplied flag
or time history, and the logical failure event. Relabeling a final perfect
syndrome cannot reconstruct side information that the model discarded.

Reinforcement-learning circuit discovery is separate again: it searches for
a preparation circuit, while a decoder interprets the record produced by the
chosen circuit. The 2026-08-02 literature sweep found no basis for renaming
the circuit-search procedure itself as the decoder.

## 5. No intrinsic fixed-block threshold

The constructor has no size parameter and always returns the same
distance-three block. An asymptotic threshold requires a sequence whose
distance grows, a noise normalization, an extraction protocol, a decoder,
and a fitted logical observable. A concatenation level, a growing quantum
Reed–Muller family, or a complete factory family could supply such a scaling
variable; the bare block cannot.

As of the 2026-08-02 decoder sweep, no fetched source supports an intrinsic
asymptotic threshold for the single `[[15,1,3]]` lookup decoder. This packet
therefore reports no threshold, pseudo-threshold, or one-point logical rate.

## 6. Minimal contract for a future circuit claim

A comparable circuit-level row must name:

1. data block and boundary/encoding convention;
2. preparation and stabilizer-extraction circuit, including gate order;
3. data, ancilla, measurement, idle, leakage, and correlation assumptions;
4. the syndrome, flag, detector, or conversion history given to the decoder;
5. decoder algorithm, postprocessing, stopping rule, and version;
6. correction or Pauli-frame semantics and the logical failure observable;
7. whether the reported quantity is a threshold, pseudo-threshold,
   one-point logical rate, bound, or hardware result.

Without that tuple, a number cannot be attached honestly to this check
matrix.

documents.title: Quantum Reed–Muller `[[15,1,3]]` — Level-2 map
documents.markdown:
# Quantum Reed–Muller `[[15,1,3]]` — Level-2 map

This index separates five statements that are often compressed into “the
fifteen-qubit code has transversal T.” They have different proofs and
different provenance.

1. [From punctured Boolean evaluations to a CSS block](punctured-evaluation-css.md):
   the declared qubit order, four coordinate rows, ten-row orthogonal
   complement, commutation, and encoded dimension.
2. [Logical quotient and sector distances](logical-quotient-and-distance.md):
   the exact X and Z normalizer quotients, the three-point logical-Z lines,
   and why `d_X=7`, `d_Z=3`, and total `d=3` are compatible.
3. [Triorthogonality and the logical phase convention](transversal-phase.md):
   every pair/triple overlap, both logical-coset weight enumerators, and the
   derivation of physical T as logical `T^dagger`.
4. [Perfect syndromes versus circuit decoding](decoding-and-circuits.md):
   the two single-error tables, extraction side information, flagged
   preparation, conversion syndromes, and the boundary around AutDEC/BP-OSD.
5. [Distillation, switching, and realization ledger](distillation-switching-realizations.md):
   the exact idealized 15-to-1 accept/error enumerator, protocol costs, and
   what the trapped-ion and neutral-atom demonstrations do and do not prove.

## Reproduction contract

Run from the repository root:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
python atlas/quantum_reed_muller_15/pedagogy/reproduce.py
make verify-entry E=atlas/quantum_reed_muller_15
```

`reproduce.py` loads the shipped constructor and asserts the qubit labels,
exact X and Z matrices, ranks, commutation, CSS parameters, exact total
distance, both sector distances, logical representatives, syndrome columns,
row-space and logical-coset weight enumerators, all pair/triple overlap
parities, logical T-versus-`T^dagger` phase, idealized distillation enumerator,
scene/check correspondence, and T3 packet state. The ordinary entry verifier
independently checks `instances.yaml`.

The card has no `construction:` operation tree because the current replay
registry has no Boolean-evaluation/puncturing adapter. The deterministic
constructor plus this independent transcript therefore verify the exact
presentation, while a future generic adapter remains a capability gap. The
broader canonical-presentation problem is tracked by
`wanted:code-equivalence`; operation-level certification beyond the existing
triorthogonality predicate is tracked by `wanted:transversal-gate-cert`.

## Provenance split

- **Recomputed facts:** the ordered nonzero-vector labels; all check rows and
  ranks; CSS commutation; `[[15,1,3]]`; `d_X=7` and `d_Z=3`; the thirty-five
  weight-three logical-Z supports; stabilizer, normalizer, and logical-coset
  weight enumerators; the pair/triple overlap ledger; physical-T logical
  phase; the idealized independent-phase-error accept and failure
  polynomials; and the exact incidence scene.
- **Bounded facts:** none. The fixed instance is small enough for exact CSS
  distance enumeration, and no seeded search is used.
- **Literature claims:** the historical Reed–Muller construction; the
  tetrahedral 3D color-code, doubled-code, tensor-network, and XP
  dictionaries; fault tolerance and resource costs of specific distillation,
  switching, flag-preparation, and AutDEC/BP-OSD protocols; and every hardware
  demonstration. These depend on a cited circuit, decoder, device, or
  representation and are not promoted to constructor-verified facts.

No threshold, pseudo-threshold, one-point logical rate, or hardware error
rate is quoted in this packet. The exact coefficient thirty-five belongs to
the explicitly stated idealized combinatorial model, not to a device or
circuit-level threshold.

documents.title: Distillation, switching, and realization ledger
documents.markdown:
# Distillation, switching, and realization ledger

> **Question.** What does the exact block algebra contribute to a universal
> protocol, and which costs or experimental conclusions remain outside it?

The transversal phase is a component, not a complete factory or universal
gate set. This page gives one exact combinatorial model and then restores the
protocol layers that model intentionally omits.

## 1. Exact idealized 15-to-1 error ledger

Consider independent phase-error bits on fifteen input resources, each equal
to one with probability `p`. Assume ideal Clifford processing and identify an
error support `e` with a Z pattern on the Reed–Muller block. The X-check
syndrome accepts exactly when

`H_X e^T = 0`,

so accepted supports are the 2048 words in `ker(H_X)`. Even accepted supports
are Z stabilizers and preserve the output logical value; odd accepted supports
are the logical-Z coset and flip it.

Using the exact enumerators from the
[distance page](logical-quotient-and-distance.md), define

```text
A(p) = (1-p)^15
     + 35 p^3 (1-p)^12
     + 105 p^4 (1-p)^11
     + 168 p^5 (1-p)^10
     + 280 p^6 (1-p)^9
     + 435 p^7 (1-p)^8
     + 435 p^8 (1-p)^7
     + 280 p^9 (1-p)^6
     + 168 p^10 (1-p)^5
     + 105 p^11 (1-p)^4
     + 35 p^12 (1-p)^3
     + p^15,

B(p) = 35 p^3 (1-p)^12
     + 168 p^5 (1-p)^10
     + 435 p^7 (1-p)^8
     + 280 p^9 (1-p)^6
     + 105 p^11 (1-p)^4
     + p^15.
```

`A(p)` is the acceptance probability in this algebraic model, and
`B(p)/A(p)` is the conditional output phase-error probability. The leading
bad term is `35 p^3`: thirty-five weight-three projective lines survive the
checks and act logically.

The reproduction script enumerates all 32768 input supports, rebuilds both
polynomials, and checks the conditional error numerically at fixed sample
values. This is not a circuit-level factory curve. No preparation faults,
Clifford faults, measurement faults, correlated inputs, routing, or decoder
latency appear in the model.

The use of this block for magic-state distillation is sourced to
[Bravyi and Kitaev](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0403025); the coefficient
and polynomial above are independently recomputed from the shipped
constructor under the stated model.

## 2. Code switching is a different use of the block

Steane and the fifteen-qubit Reed–Muller block expose complementary transversal
operations. A switching protocol:

1. embeds or interprets the current block in a common subsystem description;
2. measures checks that select the target gauge;
3. repeats or verifies those measurements according to a fault-tolerance
   rule;
4. uses the observed history to update a Pauli frame or reject the run;
5. applies the target block's transversal gate;
6. optionally reverses the conversion.

This converts a logical state, not merely a matrix file. The conversion
syndrome and conditional correction are part of the logical operation.
[Anderson, Duclos-Cianci, and Poulin](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.2734)
give explicit bidirectional fault-tolerant conversion;
[Bravyi and Cross](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.03239) explain the doubled
color-code/gauge-fixing structure; and
[Paetznick and Reichardt](https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.3709) place transversal
layers and error correction inside a universal protocol.

The abstract cost recorded on the card therefore includes conversion,
syndrome extraction, conditional correction, and a trip through Steane for H.
It does not call H a transversal gate of the unchanged Reed–Muller block.

## 3. Resource-changing neighbors

Nearby constructions answer different questions:

| construction | what changes | what must be recomputed |
|---|---|---|
| doubled/gauge-fixed color code | qubits, gauge group, and measured checks | block size, gauge/stabilizer ranks, conversion faults |
| concatenated Steane/Reed–Muller | nesting level and gate partition | total qubits, effective distance, gadgets, decoder |
| morphed descendants | a region is replaced by its child code | encoded dimension, distance, and operation set |
| tensor-network tiling | many encoder tensors are contracted | global stabilizers, logicals, geometry, and distance |

These are not equivalent relabelings of the fifteen-qubit stabilizer matrix.
The variants sweep ties the first three distinctions to
[doubled codes](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.03239),
[concatenation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.3310), and
[morphing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.01446). The tensor view is sourced to
[Quantum Lego](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.08158).

## 4. Demonstrated capability ledger

| work | platform | demonstrated boundary | not established by that result |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Daguerre et al. (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.14169) | trapped ions | preparation of a fifteen-qubit logical resource, Reed–Muller-to-Steane switching, and certification of the accepted logical magic state | increasing-distance Reed–Muller memory scaling or a circuit-independent switching rate |
| [Bluvstein et al. (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20661) | reconfigurable neutral atoms | use of 3D fifteen-qubit blocks as teleportation and arbitrary-angle-synthesis resources inside a larger architecture with other codes and qubit reuse | a bare-block memory threshold or a claim that all architecture overhead belongs to this code |

Both rows are operation-level demonstrations. Neither varies a Reed–Muller
distance parameter, because this constructor has none. The realization sweep
also found no superconducting implementation of this fifteen-qubit block in
its stated searches as of 2026-08-02. The neutral-atom paper's current fetched
title is retained in the reference registry; an earlier title is recorded as
title drift, not as a second work.

## 5. Quantitative-claim audit

This page contains one quantitative model and no device performance number:

1. **Code and boundary:** the fixed punctured four-variable `[[15,1,3]]`
   block in the constructor's qubit/logical convention.
2. **Scaling variable and observable:** input phase-error probability `p` and
   conditional accepted logical phase-error probability `B(p)/A(p)`.
3. **Circuit or schedule:** ideal Clifford reduction to the block's X-check
   acceptance equations; no physical extraction schedule is modeled.
4. **Noise and normalization:** independent identically distributed input Z
   errors, one Bernoulli trial per input resource.
5. **Decoder/postprocessing:** accept zero X syndrome; classify accepted odd
   kernel words as logical Z; exact enumeration version `qrm15-distillation-enumerator-v1`.
6. **Source location:** protocol role from Bravyi–Kitaev; coefficients
   recomputed from `constructor.H_X` and the logical parity quotient.
7. **Claim type:** exact finite-block combinatorial model, not a threshold,
   pseudo-threshold, one-point device rate, or circuit-level bound.

A future factory benchmark must replace the idealized circuit line with a
versioned preparation/extraction circuit and retain all physical fault
locations, acceptance rules, decoder inputs, and logical observables.

documents.title: Logical quotient and sector distances
documents.markdown:
# Logical quotient and sector distances

> **Question.** Why does the scalar label `[[15,1,3]]` hide a seven-versus-three
> asymmetry between logical X and logical Z?

Let `L=row(H_X)` and `G=L+span{1}` as on the
[construction page](punctured-evaluation-css.md). The CSS normalizer splits
into two classical quotient problems.

## 1. X normalizers and the logical-X coset

An X-support vector `x` commutes with every Z stabilizer exactly when
`x in S_Z^perp`. Since `S_Z=G^perp`, finite-dimensional duality gives

`S_Z^perp = G = L + span{1}`.

Quotienting by X stabilizers `L` leaves two cosets: the trivial coset `L` and
the logical coset `1+L`. Complete enumeration gives

| X coset | weights and multiplicities |
|---|---|
| `L` | weight 0: 1 word; weight 8: 15 words |
| `1+L` | weight 7: 15 words; weight 15: 1 word |

The constructor declares the all-one representative, but multiplying it by
any nonzero X stabilizer replaces it by the complement of a weight-eight word
and reduces its weight to seven. Therefore the pure-X distance is

`d_X=7`.

The logical-basis routine selects `XXXXXXX________` in its deterministic
symplectic Gram–Schmidt convention; it is in the same coset as the all-one
operator.

## 2. Z normalizers as zero-sum label sets

A Z-support vector `z` commutes with all four X checks when

`H_X z^T = 0`.

The four syndrome bits are the coordinate-wise XOR of all labels in the
support. Thus `z` is a Z normalizer exactly when its selected nonzero vectors
sum to `0000`.

The Z stabilizer space imposes one further condition: `z dot 1=0`, meaning
the support size is even. Consequently:

- even zero-sum supports are Z stabilizers;
- odd zero-sum supports are the nontrivial logical-Z coset.

This parity quotient has dimension one, matching the encoded-qubit count.

## 3. Exact lower and upper bounds meet at three

**No weight one.** A one-point support sums to its nonzero label, not to zero.

**No weight two.** Two labels sum to zero over `F_2` only when they are equal,
but a binary support cannot contain the same coordinate twice.

**A weight-three witness.** For distinct nonzero labels `a` and `b`, the third
label `a+b` is nonzero and distinct from both. The support

`{a,b,a+b}`

sums to zero and has odd cardinality, so it commutes with every X check but is
not a Z stabilizer. In the declared order, `{0001,0010,0011}` gives
`ZZZ____________`.

The lower exclusion and upper witness prove `d_Z=3`. There are exactly
thirty-five such three-point supports: each two-dimensional subspace of
`F_2^4` contains precisely its three nonzero points, and the Gaussian binomial
count is

`((2^4-1)(2^4-2))/((2^2-1)(2^2-2)) = 35`.

The reproduction transcript also enumerates all `C(15,3)` supports and finds
the same thirty-five witnesses without relying on that counting formula.

## 4. Total distance and error correction

For a CSS code, a minimum logical Pauli may be chosen pure X or pure Z, so

`d = min(d_X,d_Z) = min(7,3) = 3`.

The exact verifier searches supports in increasing weight, tests both CSS
sectors, and returns `(3, exact-css-enum)`. This establishes correction of an
arbitrary single-qubit Pauli error. It does not establish comparable logical
rates in the two sectors under biased noise: rates also depend on the decoder,
syndrome circuit, and physical error distribution.

## 5. Full Z-normalizer enumerator

The kernel of `H_X` has dimension eleven and therefore contains 2048 support
vectors. Exact enumeration separates it by parity:

| coset | weight enumerator |
|---|---|
| Z stabilizers | `1 + 105 y^4 + 280 y^6 + 435 y^8 + 168 y^10 + 35 y^12` |
| logical Z | `35 y^3 + 168 y^5 + 435 y^7 + 280 y^9 + 105 y^11 + y^15` |

The two rows each contain 1024 words. The odd row becomes the logical-error
numerator in the idealized distillation model on the
[protocol ledger](distillation-switching-realizations.md). These coefficients
are constructor-derived facts; no experimental or circuit-level rate is
being inferred from them.

documents.title: From punctured Boolean evaluations to a CSS block
documents.markdown:
# From punctured Boolean evaluations to a CSS block

> **Question.** How do fifteen four-bit labels determine the complete
> stabilizer space, rather than merely suggest a Reed–Muller analogy?

Everything below uses the constructor's fixed order: qubit `q` carries the
four-bit binary expansion of `q+1`, from `0001` through `1111`, with the
most-significant bit first.

## 1. The evaluation map

Let `V=F_2^4` and `V*=V\{0}`. For `u in F_2^4`, define the length-fifteen word

`ell_u = (u dot v)_(v in V*)`.

The map `u -> ell_u` is linear and injective. If `ell_u` vanished for every
nonzero `v`, then it would vanish on the four standard basis vectors and
force `u=0`. Its image

`L = {ell_u : u in F_2^4}`

therefore has dimension four. The constructor uses the four coordinate
functions as an ordered basis:

```text
000000011111111
000111100001111
011001100110011
101010101010101
```

Every nonzero `ell_u` has weight eight. On all sixteen inputs a nonzero linear
functional has an eight-dimensional zero half and an eight-dimensional one
half; its value at the removed input `0000` is zero, so puncturing does not
change the weight.

This Boolean-evaluation starting point is the route given by Steane's
[quantum Reed–Muller construction](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9608026).
The Atlas fixes an explicit basis and coordinate order so every later
statement is executable.

## 2. Why the all-one row is logical, not a check

Let `1` be the length-fifteen all-one word. It is not in `L`: the zero word in
`L` has weight zero and every nonzero word has weight eight, while `1` has
weight fifteen. Hence

`G = L + span{1}`

has dimension five. The code uses `L` as its X-stabilizer space and reserves
the other coset `1+L` for logical X. This choice is essential. If the odd row
were also declared an X stabilizer, the encoded dimension and diagonal phase
action would both change.

## 3. Build Z checks by orthogonality

Define

`S_Z = G^perp = {z : z dot ell_u = 0 for all u, and z dot 1 = 0}`.

The constructor obtains an ordered basis with
`gf2.nullspace(vstack([X_CHECKS, LOGICAL_X]))`. Its ten output rows are a
basis of `S_Z`, not ten individually canonical geometric faces. Any invertible
row recombination gives the same Z-stabilizer group.

Because `S_Z` is orthogonal to `L`,

`H_X H_Z^T = 0`.

Thus every X generator commutes with every Z generator. Same-type generators
already commute, so `CheckMatrix.from_css(H_X,H_Z)` is a valid stabilizer
matrix. The verifier checks this product and calls `validate()` on the full
symplectic array.

The extra condition `z dot 1=0` says every Z stabilizer has even support. It
also distinguishes Z stabilizers from the odd logical-Z coset used on the
[distance page](logical-quotient-and-distance.md).

## 4. Count the encoded dimension

The X rank is four. Since `G` has dimension five in a fifteen-dimensional
ambient space, `S_Z=G^perp` has dimension ten. X-only and Z-only stabilizer
rows occupy disjoint symplectic halves, so their ranks add:

`rank(S)=4+10=14`.

A rank-fourteen stabilizer on fifteen qubits encodes

`k=15-14=1`.

This count is independent of the particular nullspace basis printed in
`constructor.py`. It depends only on the evaluation space `L` and the reserved
all-one row.

## 5. Relation to the fifteen-qubit quantum Hamming block

The repository's `[[15,7,3]]` quantum Hamming entry uses the same four
coordinate rows for both X and Z checks. Its four-dimensional Z space is a
subspace of this code's ten-dimensional `S_Z`. Adding six independent Z
constraints fixes six of the Hamming block's seven logical degrees of freedom
and leaves this one-qubit block. The companion entry verifies that literal
row-space containment in the shared qubit order.

This relation is gauge-out/dimension reduction, not two names for the same
stabilizer code. The ranks `8` and `14` already rule out that conflation.

## 6. What is and is not verified here

The evaluation points, matrices, ranks, commutation, and encoded dimension are
recomputed by `pedagogy/reproduce.py`. The historical naming and the fact that
this block is the punctured four-variable member of the broader quantum
Reed–Muller lineage remain cited to the primary literature. The tetrahedral
3D color-code realization is a separate curated dictionary; the present proof
uses no unexported geometric assumption.

# Triorthogonality and the logical phase convention

> **Question.** Which property beyond CSS commutation makes a bitwise T-type
> phase preserve this code, and why does the answer contain a dagger?

CSS commutation tests overlaps between an X-check row and a Z-check row.
Diagonal phase gates instead test how X-stabilizer codewords overlap with one
another. The relevant five-row matrix is

`G = [1; H_X]`,

where the first row is the odd all-one logical-X representative and the last
four rows are even X stabilizers.

## 1. Pair and triple overlap ledger

Index the rows by `g_0=1` and the four coordinate functions
`g_1,...,g_4`.

- `|g_0 and g_i|=8`: a coordinate function is one at eight labels.
- `|g_i and g_j|=4` for distinct coordinates: fixing two bits to one leaves
  four choices for the other bits.
- `|g_0 and g_i and g_j|=4`: intersecting with the all-one row changes
  nothing.
- `|g_i and g_j and g_k|=2` for distinct coordinates: fixing three bits
  leaves two choices for the fourth.

All pair and triple overlaps are even. This is the triorthogonality condition
of [Bravyi and Haah](https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.2426). The Atlas predicate
`transversal_t_candidate(H_X, LOGICAL_X)` recomputes all ten pair tests and
all ten triple tests on the shipped matrix.

Triorthogonality is stronger than the pairwise CSS relation. The Steane
matrix, for example, has an odd three-row intersection and fails this test
despite defining a valid self-dual CSS code.

## 2. Stabilizer codewords have weight zero modulo eight

The X-stabilizer space `L` contains the zero word and the fifteen nonzero
linear functions. Their exact weight enumerator is

`W_L(y) = 1 + 15 y^8`.

Define the encoded computational basis using the X-stabilizer superpositions

`|0_L> = (1/4) sum_(x in L) |x>`

and

`|1_L> = X(1)|0_L> = (1/4) sum_(x in L) |1+x>`.

Every component of `|0_L>` has weight zero modulo eight. Hence bitwise
physical T, whose phase on `|x>` is `exp(i pi |x|/4)`, assigns the common
phase one to the entire logical-zero state.

## 3. The logical-one coset has weight seven modulo eight

Complementing the zero word gives weight fifteen; complementing any
weight-eight word gives weight seven. Therefore

`W_(1+L)(y) = y^15 + 15 y^7`,

and every logical-one component has weight seven modulo eight. Physical
`T^otimes 15` supplies the common phase

`exp(i pi 7/4) = exp(-i pi/4)`.

In the ordered basis `(|0_L>,|1_L>)`, the induced operation is therefore

`diag(1, exp(-i pi/4)) = T^dagger`.

The inverse physical layer, `(T^dagger)^otimes 15`, implements logical T.
This derivation fixes the card's convention. Replacing a bare statement
“transversal T” with this phase calculation prevents two sources using
conjugate magic-state conventions from appearing to disagree.

## 4. Why signs and phases matter

The sign-free binary symplectic matrix establishes supports, commutation, and
logical Pauli quotients. It does not retain the eighth-root phases introduced
by T. That is why the reproduction transcript explicitly enumerates
computational-basis weights in addition to running a triorthogonality
predicate.

An XP-stabilizer representation can keep this phase data in one algebraic
object; [Webster, Brown, and Bartlett](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.00103)
provide that broader formalism. The Atlas still treats XP as a curated
dictionary here because the ordinary constructor exports a Pauli
`CheckMatrix`, not a phase-aware XP object.

## 5. Other transversal and non-transversal operations

**CNOT.** Pairwise physical CNOT between identically ordered CSS blocks
preserves the two stabilizer groups and induces logical CNOT. The support
conjugation is exact at the check-matrix level; routing and recovery are
separate circuit costs.

**Hadamard.** Bitwise H exchanges X and Z. Here their ranks are four and ten,
so H cannot map the unchanged stabilizer group to itself. The card therefore
does not call H transversal. Its cited H route switches to the Steane code,
uses Steane's transversal H, then switches back.

**Universality.** T-type phase plus CNOT is not a complete native
fault-tolerant instruction set for one unchanged block. The cited universal
constructions add error correction, code switching, state preparation,
measurement, or another encoded block. The
[protocol ledger](distillation-switching-realizations.md) accounts for those
resources instead of charging them to transversality.

## 6. Certification boundary

The pair/triple overlaps and logical diagonal phase are fully recomputed for
this fixed constructor. The operations facet remains literature-originated
because the repository does not yet certify complete logical gate sets,
fault propagation, or circuit gadgets. That larger capability is tracked by
`wanted:transversal-gate-cert`; the current exact proxy is the narrow
triorthogonality and coset-phase calculation used here.
